newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIAN CRICKET BOARD NAMES NEW CEO.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIAN CRICKET BOARD NAMES NEW CEO.

text.p: The Australian Cricket Board (ACB) said on Friday that lawyer Malcolm Speed would be its new chief executive to replace Graham Halbish, who was sacked in January after a dispute with board members.

Speed, 48, is executive chairman of the Australian national basketball league but said he would resign from that post. With an extensive background in sports administration, Speed was a keen club cricketer for about 20 years.

"The Australian Cricket Board is delighted it has been able to appoint someone of outstanding quality and the board looks forward to working with Mr Speed in facing the many challenges that Australian and world cricket will confront in the future," ACB chairman Denis Rogers said in a statement.
Speed's predecessor Halbish left his post in January and reached an out-of-court settlement with the ACB after suing them for unfair dismissal.
Halbish is now involved in another dispute with the ACB, which refuses to accept him as the representative of the newly-formed Australian Cricketers' Association in pay negotiations.

Speed said he will not join the Australia team when they leave on Saturday for their six-test Ashes tour of Englsand but added he would attend an International Cricket Council meeting in Britain later in the year.
He added it was important for cricket administrators to address new issues and for the game to change with the times.
"Cricket has a very traditional following, but we've also got to look at ways of accomodating new generations of cricket followers," Speed told reporters.
